turns.text: Hi there — I'm Sarah, an AI researcher with HeliumDeploy. Thank you so much for taking 25 minutes to do this — it really means a lot. Honestly, the more you can share with me, the better — we're aiming for about fifteen hundred words of feedback together, so please don't worry about going long. The founders read every word of these chats, so what you say actually shapes what HD does next. As a thank-you you'll get a $75 discount code at the end. So — to kick us off, tell me about your mining setup right now. What are you running, where, and what are you trying to figure out next?
I have one of the BIDAC six o ones. And I have a couple apps on my phone. Yes. That one. And everything I do, I try and incorporate, and I'm looking to try and upgrade now.

Nice — the Bitaxe Gamma 601. Let me pull it up so we're on the same page. So you've got the Gamma running and you're thinking about an upgrade. Tell me about the apps on your phone — what are you using, and what are you watching with them?
The apps on my phone are Go mining and things like that. The B. miner, I've got it hooked to my computer so I can do things carefully and safely and see what I'm doing.

Got it — so Go Mining plus the Bitaxe hooked into your computer so you can watch what's happening carefully. That's interesting — "carefully and safely" — say more about that. What are you being careful about?

Well, I have another Bed Axe Miner but it is not functioning properly. It's supposed to be a three terahertz miner, And when it connects, it goes up to six hundred something terabytes, then it drops down, then it goes back up to four hundred. And, eventually, it overheats the power supply, and I can't do anything with it.

Oh wow — okay, so you have a *second* Bitaxe that's basically broken. Supposed to be 3 TH/s, spiking weirdly, overheating the power supply. That's frustrating. Where did you get that second one from — was that from HD or somewhere else?
It was from somewhere else.
Got it. Without naming names if you don't want to — was it AliExpress, eBay, or one of the other shops? Trying to understand where folks are landing when they shop around.
Uh, I bought it several years ago now, and it started out, it was working well until recently. So I don't remember exactly where I bought it. I bought your Biddex from Amazon.
Ah okay — so your *working* Bitaxe Gamma you actually bought through Amazon, not directly from heliumdeploy.com. Interesting. What made you go through Amazon for it instead of the HD site directly?
I had some built up credit, and I wanted to use up the credit.

Makes total sense — burn the Amazon credit, smart move. So now you're thinking about an upgrade. What's drawing you in — are you wanting more hashrate, or is it more about replacing the broken one, or something else entirely?

Actually, all above. I'm looking to upgrade my hash rate to have a little bit better income plus, of course, replace the broken one because it it's running, but it's not producing anything. And I like to have someone I can actually get in contact with. Because getting stuff through Amazon, you can't always get ahold of the manufacturer.

That last bit — "I like to have someone I can actually get in contact with" — that's a big one. Say more about that. Has there been a moment recently where you tried to get ahold of someone and couldn't?

Yes. On the one that is not functioning at this time, I attempted to contact and look up where I bought it, and I cannot seem to find it on any of the places that I normally purchase from. I have not been able to get ahold of the manufacturer. When I look for the manufacturer online, the company does not exist.

Oof — that's the nightmare scenario. The manufacturer literally doesn't exist anymore, and you're sitting on a dead $200+ miner with nowhere to turn. That really stings.

So now when you're shopping for the upgrade, being able to reach a human is a real filter for you. Have you actually reached out to HD yet — emailed, chatted, anything — or are you still in the research phase?

Still researching. I've been looking at the site. And I admit it. I've been comparing prices because once again, I have some Amazon credit built up, but I see that you are having multiple discounts. On your site. So I'm kinda comparing each

Totally fair — Amazon credit is real money. Let me pull up the homepage so we can look at the lineup together. There's a comparison table on the homepage — I just scrolled you to it. Did you come across this when you were poking around the site?

Yes. I did. I was actually getting some matched up and trying to figure out which ones I was gonna go with. Price is a factor. I am not a well off individual, so I'm looking at the lower ends. At least until I can build up some money in and reinvest it.

Got it — building up gradually, reinvesting as you go. Smart way to play it.

So when you were on this table, which row were you actually leaning toward? Were you eyeing the NerdQaxe at $249, or staying down at the Gamma level?
I was actually looking at both of those. Uh, right now, unfortunately, all I can afford the gamma level.

Yep, that's real. So Gamma is the now-purchase, NerdQaxe is the someday.

Let me ask — when you were comparing the two on that table, what was the thing that made the NerdQaxe attractive enough to be on your wishlist? Was it the hashrate jump, or something else about it?
The nerd q x I really like the hash tag jump. But it's almost five times the price. So if I bought five of the smaller ones, I would still have more terra hashes than I would by buying one big one.

Oh, that's a sharp piece of math — five Gammas at $95 gets you 7.5 TH/s for $475, versus one NerdQaxe at $249 for 6 TH/s. You'd actually beat it on hashrate AND have redundancy.

So is that genuinely how you're thinking about it — stack Gammas one at a time as you can afford them? Like, is the plan to end up with a little fleet of five Bitaxes?
Yes. The plan is to do that. But according to the comparison chart you just put up, the gamma, Betx Gamma is on sale for fifty nine dollars. Instead of ninety five. That's the other draw right now.

Oh nice catch — yeah, $59 vs $95 is a real discount. That changes the math even more — five of them at $59 is $295, basically the same as one NerdQaxe but you get 7.5 TH/s instead of 6.

So if you pulled the trigger today on one Gamma at $59 — where would it live? Like, physically in your house, where does it go?
I have a small office that I would put it in, and it would be in a room all by itself. Lonesome with my work computer and printer.

Got it — dedicated little office space, just you, the work computer, the printer, and the miner. That's a nice setup.

Question on that — your current Gamma that's running. Is it in that same office? And how do you feel about the noise of it in there while you're working?

Actually, no. It's in my bedroom, uh, long as I leave it at default settings in the XOS, is very quiet. I can barely tell it's on. And it's it's supposed to be a one point something terahertz and I wanna say it's doing one point two. So I'm pretty pleased with what it's doing.

Oh that's great — running quiet in the bedroom at 1.2 TH/s, you're basically getting what the box promised. Love that.

You said "as long as I leave it at default settings in AxeOS" — that's interesting wording. Have you played with the settings at all? Tried overclocking it or messing with voltage?

Yes. I have. I've tried, uh, in the XOS. I've increased and decreased the power going each direction. If you go one step above default, the fan increases greatly right off the bat. So I've left it in default since it's quiet, and it doesn't use quite as much electricity.

Smart — you tested it, learned where the fan-noise cliff is, and dialed back. That's exactly the right move for a bedroom unit.

So you're already in AxeOS poking around. Where do you go to learn about that stuff — like when you wanted to know "what happens if I bump the voltage" — is that YouTube, Discord, Reddit, somewhere else?

Somewhere else, I have been working on computers and stuff for over thirty years. I tend to be a trial and error style person. I will go in and play with settings and see what they do. And hopefully figure out what makes whatever the device is work the best.

Thirty years of trial-and-error — I love that. You're just going in and feeling it out. That tracks with you saying earlier you do things "carefully" — you're testing one variable at a time.

So when something gets really stuck, like your dead Bitaxe with the wild hashrate spikes — you didn't go ask a Discord or a forum? You just kept poking at it yourself until you decided it's broken?

Yes. I kept poking at it. I have tried different firmware updates I've even backed it down several firmware updates. But, again, it was working fine. Now all of a sudden, it is not. So So I'm afraid it may have been the company that made it. There may be a flow in the system where the board or the processor that I cannot do anything about?

Yeah, that's a heartbreaker — you did all the right things, flashed forward, rolled back, and it's still flaky. Sounds like silicon-level failure, nothing you can fix from software.

Quick sidestep — let me show you something we're researching and see if it lands for you. HD is thinking about selling a little Ethernet adapter that snaps onto a Bitaxe so you can run it wired instead of WiFi — about $35. For your current setup in the bedroom, is wired-vs-WiFi something you've thought about at all?
No. But I do have several ports left on my router. So it would be a good option. Plus in my office, I have an a router extender with several ports on it also.
Got it — so you've got Ethernet ports ready to go in both rooms. At $35 added on top of a $59 Gamma — would that feel like a fair add-on, or does it start to push the math the wrong way for you?
That depends. Is the Ethernet adapter a one gig? Or what speed is it?

Honest answer — I don't have the exact spec in front of me, but the chip it's based on (Wiznet W5500) is a 100 Mbit Ethernet controller, not gigabit. For mining traffic it's massively more than you'd ever need — pool communication is tiny — but if you were hoping for gigabit, this wouldn't be it.

Does that matter to you?
Now that you've explained that it doesn't take as much bandwidth to do the mining, no. It doesn't. That just gives me more options.

Perfect — and yeah, mining traffic is basically nothing, kilobytes a minute.

Okay, let me ask you something different. You mentioned earlier you have Go Mining and "things like that" on your phone. What else are you running — what's the rest of the app stack you check on?

There are several different apps for mining Most of them, you have to watch ads all day long to get anything from them. With the Go mining app, all I have to do is hit service once a day. And, yes, I have made a small investment there. The other ones I am finding are not exactly secure. I have found a couple that I have reached their threshold. And tried to withdraw, and nothing happens.

Oh that's rough — you hit the withdrawal threshold and the money just… doesn't come out. So you're learning the hard way which apps are scams.

That actually connects back to something you said earlier — "I like to have someone I can actually get in contact with." Sounds like that's a real theme for you across everything Bitcoin-related, not just the hardware. Is that fair?
Yes. It is. I also use Crypto dot com as my exchange. So I have had to reach out to them several times, and they have always gotten back with me.

Got it — Crypto.com has earned your trust because they actually answer. That's a real bar.

So if you do pull the trigger and buy from HD — what would "good support" look like to you? Like, if six months from now your new Gamma started acting up the way your old Bitaxe did, what would you need from HD to feel like you made the right choice?

Well, from what I can see, you've already got a well set up page where I can just hit support, and I can ask questions and etcetera, tell them what I've done, and ask them what suggestions they have to succeed on repairing the device or if I need to replace certain components or if it can be sent in and be repaired.

Got it — so what you actually want is a real back-and-forth: tell them what you've already tried, get real suggestions, and have an option to send it in if it's beyond home-fixing. Repair, not just refund.

That's interesting — most folks just want a replacement. You'd actually rather have it repaired. Why is that?

Well, my main job is Dell warranty repair. If your Dell computer breaks and you have the right warranty, they send me parts. I come to your business or home, and I repair your system. So I'm in the repair line of work.

Oh that's a great piece of context — you literally do warranty repair for a living. So you think about hardware the way a repair tech does: parts, not replacements. That makes total sense now.

Does that show up in how you bought the Bitaxe in the first place? Like, were you looking at it thinking "I could fix this myself if something goes wrong"?

Parts of it, yes. For example, the fan and the heat sink, are very similar to the fans and the heat sinks on smaller laptops and older laptops, actually. The newer ones are a lot thinner than what's on here, but they're also have more circumference. And it doesn't look like, honestly, there's much that can be repaired on one of these. Most of the components are soldered on, and soldering that small is something I'm not good at.

Yeah — surface-mount soldering at that scale is a different sport. You can swap fans and heatsinks all day, but a BGA chip? Not happening on a kitchen table.

So if HD sold replacement fans, heatsinks, maybe alternate power supplies as accessories — would you actually buy those? Or do you just pull them off old laptops you have lying around?

Actually, size wise, they're different. So, yes, I would gladly buy them from HD. Would make my life simpler if I need one. So far, I haven't burned a fan up so I'm rather impressed on how well they survive.

Good to know — so spare fans, heatsinks, PSUs from HD is a real "yes" for you. That's useful.

Let me push on one more thing — the broken Bitaxe. You said it overheats the power supply. Is the PSU it came with, or did you swap to a different one? And do you think that's where the failure actually is — the PSU rather than the board?

I don't think it's the power supply unit because in the x OS, you can watch the power usage. And as it goes up in t h, it raises the power, and the power limit's only a hundred and fifty watts on this power supply. And, again, that was for three terahertz, but this one's hitting four hundred terahertz consistently So I think it is a setting inside that is not set properly, and it's allowing it to get too high.

Interesting — so you're watching the AxeOS dashboard, you see hashrate spike to 400+ TH/s when it should be 3, and the wattage is climbing right with it until the PSU taps out at 150W. So it's not the PSU failing — it's the board telling the chip to run way harder than it should.

That kinda sounds like a corrupted setting or firmware bug, not silicon. Have you tried a full factory reset / nvram wipe on it?

I don't know how to do a factor reset yet. That is one of the things I'm researching. Again, I have just learned how to do the firmware updates. So I don't know if I'm smart enough to do a factory reset. And since I can't find any information online about this particular model, it makes it a little more difficult.

Yeah — and that's the crux, right? With your working Gamma you can google "Bitaxe Gamma factory reset" and get answers. With the dead one from the vanished company, you're flying blind because the documentation doesn't exist anywhere.

That actually circles back to a really strong reason to buy from HD next time — you get a live human plus a model that other people actually own and talk about online.

Okay, let me ask one more thing and then we'll start wrapping. You mentioned earlier you'd love to scale up — five Gammas eventually. What's the dream end-state? Like, is this about earning income, or is it about something else?

I would like to scale up and eventually have this as part of my passive income. I'm up to, uh, about thirty dollars a week in my Go Mining app. So if I can get this one up and reinvest into it, or I can get some more out of it also, and reinvest in it while I'm still able to work Eventually, I would like to be able to not have to work.

That's a real goal — passive income runway so you don't *have* to keep doing Dell repair forever. Thirty bucks a week on Go Mining is a real start, and stacking Gammas one at a time fits that strategy.

This has been really helpful, honestly. Before we wrap — is there anything you wanted to share that I didn't ask about? Anything about HD, the products, the experience, that's on your mind?
No. I'm still researching the site. I just recently digging So I have a lot more research to do and a lot more things to look into.

Totally fair — you're early in the research, taking your time, comparing the math. That's exactly the right way to do it given where you are.

Real quick before you go — your $75 discount code will come through email at (email hidden) within the next day or so. With the Gamma at $59 right now plus that code, you'd be in really good shape to grab your first one.

Thank you so much for the time and the honesty — the broken-miner story, the Dell repair context, the passive-income goal — all of that is genuinely useful. The founders will read every word.

Take care, and good luck with the build-out.
Thank you.
You're very welcome — have a wonderful day.
Is there anything else I need to do, or may I hang up now?
You're all done — nothing else needed on your end. The discount code will land in your inbox. Take care.
